articles.title: 'Baseless lawsuits': MEA rejects US court summonses to NSA Ajit Doval
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday rejected US court summonses issued to National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and former Research
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday rejected US court summonses issued to National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and former Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) chief Samant Goel in a civil lawsuit filed by pro-Khalistan outfit Sikhs for Justice (SFJ). Responding to a question on a US court ordering the delivery of the summonses through Delhi courts, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, "We reject such baseless lawsuits."A US district court has ordered the alternative delivery of judicial documents to Doval and Goel through three district courts in Delhi, Patiala House, Dwarka and Tis Hazari. The Clerk of the US Court has been directed to send the documents through international mail or courier.The order was issued by Judge Katherine Polk Failla of the US district court for the Southern District of New York in a civil lawsuit filed by Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, founder of SFJ.What the US court order saysThe court said it had attempted to serve the summonses through India's central authority under the Hague Convention, but the attempt was rejected. It subsequently authorised alternative service under Article 19 of the Hague Convention and India's Code of Civil Procedure.“The court respectfully requests the assistance of receiving Indian courts in effecting service of process upon the defendants in this civil action pending before this court,” the order stated.However, sources said the summonses were not binding and described the court's move as a “routine, procedural step”.Earlier, the summonses had been delivered through the Indian embassy by the US state department, which clarified that the action did not reflect any position on the case.This is not the first time SFJ has filed a civil lawsuit in the US against an Indian political figure. In 2013, former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh was served with a civil summons in a suit filed by the outfit, which alleged human rights violations linked to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Bath Christmas art trail features characters from The Snowman
articles.summary: A trail that includes 12 sculptures from the children's book The Snowman is unveiled in Bath.
articles.body:
Giant sculptures of the much-loved children's book character The Snowman have been placed across a city for an art trail.

The Snowman Trail, led by Bath BID, Wild In Art and Penguin Ventures, will see 12 sculptures, each representing a verse from The Twelve Days of Christmas.

The project supports the Bath Play Project, which provides inclusive play-based services for children and families across Bath and North East Somerset.

Allison Herbert, CEO of Bath BID, said she hopes it encourages visitors to explore the "beautiful city", discover new places and "enjoy a little flurry of festive joy ahead of the Christmas market".

"This much-loved character has captured hearts for generations, and we're excited to create a trail that encourages people to explore our beautiful city, discover new places and enjoy a little flurry of festive joy ahead of the Christmas market opening," Herbert said.

"We hope the trail brings families together, encourages people to spend time in Bath and creates magical memories during the most wonderful time of the year."

Visitors following the trail can donate to Bath Play Project by scanning a QR code on the base of each sculpture.

Caroline Haworth, director of the charity, said they are "very proud" to be supported.

"We began in 1979, one year after Raymond Briggs wrote The Snowman," she said.

"The beautifully illustrated book is wordless, and therefore fully inclusive, which is our core ethos alongside our vision that every child has the right to play, supporting and enriching children's wellbeing."

articles.title: Bird flu confirmed in Berkshire with other species affected, charity says
articles.summary: The cases follow bird flu being confirmed across Berkshire earlier this year.
articles.body:
More than 20 birds have died from bird flu over the past fortnight in Berkshire, a charity has said.

Wendy Hermon, Swan Support's operations director, said it is the second wave seen in the county in 2026 after another affected birds in the winter and spring .

"Normally it hits and then it's about two years later [it returns]. I don't know what's going on... I think it's going to be a massive outbreak," she said.

Reading and West Berkshire councils have said they were aware of recent cases in their respective areas and have urged people not to touch sick or dead birds.

Swan Support is an approved body that can assess and respond to reports of affected birds.

Hermon said it was aware of swans, geese, gulls and pigeons being affected.

"Normally when we've dealt with bird flu it's been to swans and geese but it's spread so quickly into other species of birds that we have not seen [affected] before over such a quick period," she added.

The risk to public health is low and Reading Borough Council said it is monitoring areas around Rivermead Park, Caversham Bridge and Christchurch Meadows.

West Berkshire Council said it was aware of confirmed avian flu in wild birds in the borough in October and November. Both were birds of prey.

The UK Health Security Agency said people should not feed wild birds.

Dogs should be kept under close control and on leads where advised and should avoid contact with wild bird droppings and feathers.

Everyone should wash their hands thoroughly after visiting riverside areas.

Any dead wild birds in Berkshire should be reported to Swan Support.

articles.title: John D Rockefeller Jr created a trust for his granddaughter in 1943, but she later challenged JPMorgan's 1967 sale of oil stocks; a New York appeals court rejected her claim that the bank mishandled the family assets
articles.summary: A New York appeals court has rejected a legal challenge by the granddaughter of oil tycoon John D Rockefeller Jr, who accused JPMorgan Chase of
articles.body: A New York appeals court has rejected a legal challenge by the granddaughter of oil tycoon John D Rockefeller Jr, who accused JPMorgan Chase of mishandling her family trust by selling oil company stocks in 1967 and investing the proceeds in riskier securities. The court upheld a lower court's decision approving the bank's accounting of the trust and releasing it from liability over its management of the assets between 1962 and 2012.The case involved a trust established in 1943 by Rockefeller Jr for his granddaughter, Dr Lucy Rockefeller Waletzky. JPMorgan Chase, formerly known as The Chase National Bank of the City of New York, was appointed trustee under an agreement dated December 27, 1943.In its November 19 ruling, the Appellate Division of the New York Supreme Court's First Department unanimously dismissed Waletzky's objections, finding that she had failed to establish that the bank's records were incomplete or that its investment decisions were imprudent.Why Rockefeller's granddaughter challenged JPMorganUnder the terms of the trust, Waletzky was entitled to receive its accumulated net income after turning 21 in March 1962. Decades later, in 2016, she filed objections to the bank's accounting, alleging that JPMorgan had failed to maintain accurate records and breached its fiduciary duty by not investing the trust's assets prudently.A central part of her challenge concerned the bank's 1967 sale of shares in several oil companies. Waletzky argued that the decision amounted to a breach of the duty of loyalty and self-dealing because the bank had allegedly acted to benefit its own business interests rather than the trust.She claimed that the oil companies were generating unprecedented revenues and paying record dividends when their shares were sold. According to her objections, JPMorgan subsequently invested the proceeds in a collection of riskier, lower-yielding securities, including shares in companies that had business relationships with the bank.She further alleged that the bank had extended loans to some of these companies, several of the investments were eventually sold at a net loss, and the sale of the oil stocks created a substantial tax liability for the trust.Court says bank's investment strategy was prudentThe appeals court, however, found that JPMorgan had provided sufficient evidence to demonstrate that it had properly accounted for its management of the trust.The bank submitted its accounting records along with a supporting affidavit stating that the schedules of trust assets were accurate and complete. This shifted the burden to Waletzky to establish, by a preponderance of the evidence, that the accounting was incomplete or inaccurate.The court noted that witnesses for JPMorgan had testified that maintaining transaction records and investment diaries was standard industry practice when the bank managed the trust. They also said the records produced were typical and adequate. Waletzky failed to refute their testimony, the judges observed.On the investment dispute, the court found that there was sufficient evidence to support the bank's diversification strategy under the applicable standards governing trust investments.It said Waletzky had relied largely on hindsight to argue that selling the high-performing oil stocks and purchasing other securities was an imprudent decision.The judges also pointed out that the availability of other investment options did not automatically make the bank's chosen strategy imprudent. The record supported diversification even if, in retrospect, concentrating the trust's assets in oil company shares might have generated higher returns.The court also rejected the self-dealing allegation, finding that Waletzky had produced no evidence establishing that JPMorgan's business relationships with companies whose shares it purchased had influenced its investment decisions.The November 19 decision unanimously affirmed the lower court's order approving JPMorgan's accounting for the period from March 9, 1962, to June 30, 2012, and releasing the bank from liability concerning the matters covered by the accounting.You use AI every day.
